subject: Net terms exception and consolidated billing path
body:
From: Ella Shaw <ella@novahealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novahealth.com>; Finance Contact <ap@novahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Net terms exception and consolidated billing path

Chloe — thanks for the draft. A few clarifying asks from procurement/finance before legal will sign off:

- Net terms: Nova typically requires Net 60 for large vendor contracts. Can Redwood confirm any flexibility on Net 60 vs Net 30? If not, we need an approval path (who signs Net 30 exception).
- Invoicing entity: We want a single consolidated invoice to our US parent (Nova Health, Inc.). Can you confirm Redwood can invoice the US entity only and accept payment from that entity even if some services run in EU?
- VAT / sales tax: We'll attach our tax certificate; please confirm Redwood will not gross-up EU VAT into our invoice if we pay the US entity.
- Activation fee: If we agree an activation fee, we need proration for the partial first month and a line item in the order form.

Attached: Purchase paperwork and Nova tax certificate. Please advise next steps and who from Redwood legal/finance will own the exception gating.

Thanks,
Ella
Ella Shaw
Sr. Procurement Manager | Nova Health

---

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ella Shaw <ella@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Net terms exception and consolidated billing path

Ella — appreciate the clear list. Quick responses inline below and a proposed path.

1) Net terms: Our standard is Net 30. For enterprise customers we can consider Net 45 or Net 60 with a credit facility review. For Deal-3921 I recommend Net 45 as a compromise (reduces risk and is common for mid-enterprise). If Nova requires Net 60, we'll need approval from Finance + Head of Revenue (Kimberly will advise on approval authority).

2) Consolidated invoicing: We can invoice Nova Health, Inc. (US) as the billing entity and accept payment from that entity. To confirm, Redwood will need: (a) the PO referencing the billing entity, and (b) a signed orderform that lists the US entity as the invoice recipient.

3) VAT: We can accept the tax certificate and agree that Redwood will not add EU VAT to invoices to Nova Health, Inc. provided Nova's tax position is documented. Our tax team will need the certificate and entity mapping to finalize.

4) Activation / proration: We'll add an activation fee line and include a proration clause for the first invoice.

Next steps I propose:
- I attached OrderForm_NovaHealth_v2_redline.docx with the requested billing entity + activation fee clause + a Net 45 proposal.
- Kimberly: can you confirm whether Net 60 approvals are possible here or if Net 45 is the right escalation?
- Ben / Jordan: please keep procurement updated and flag if Nova can accept Net 45.

Attaching the redline now.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Commercial Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_NovaHealth_v2_redline.docx

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>; Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Net terms exception and consolidated billing path

Chloe / team — reading through the redline. Position guidance below so commercial can present a clean ask to procurement: 

- Net terms: Net 60 is high risk for us at this stage. We will allow Net 60 only against an approved credit + finance guarantee. Net 45 is acceptable without further underwriting for this cohort. If Nova insists on Net 60 as a hard requirement, we will need: (i) finance credit approval (I can route), (ii) an early-payment or service-credit clause (we typically add a 1% monthly late fee and a 30-day service-curtailment trigger on >90 days overdue), and (iii) executive sign-off.
- Billing consolidation: Acceptable. Add the billing entity name in Section 2 of the Order Form and require a PO referencing the billing entity. We'll document this as a billing-only preference and include a clause that services may run across regions.
- Taxes: Require Nova's tax certificate on file + an indemnity for tax liability if they later change remittance. We'll accept their certificate for VAT/non-VAT treatment on the US invoice.
- Activation fee proration: Good; add an explicit proration example in the appendix (first invoice = activation fee + prorated monthly subscription).

I'll draft a short approval note for Finance if Net 60 is requested. If you want to try Net 45 first, push that with procurement and let me know if they push back.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops | Redwood Inference

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ella Shaw <ella@novahealth.com>; Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Net terms exception and consolidated billing path

Ella — thanks for the packet and the certificate. Quick commercial asks so we can lock the order form today: 

- Would Nova accept Net 45 as a compromise? That gets your procurement cadence aligned and removes a major gating item for Redwood.
- We'll list Nova Health, Inc. as the invoice recipient and will accept payment from that entity (please confirm PO details and remit address).
- We will include the activation fee proration example in the order form appendix and the tax certificate will be attached to the deal file.

If you can confirm Net 45 and the PO remit details by EOD tomorrow, I'll get the final redline to Legal for signature.

Thanks — look forward to closing this.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: Ella Shaw <ella@novahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>; Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novahealth.com>; Finance Contact <ap@novahealth.com>; Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Net terms exception and consolidated billing path

Ben / Chloe — confirmed internally: Nova can accept Net 45 for the initial 12-month commitment if Redwood includes the proration and activation example in the appendix and the invoice is consolidated to Nova Health, Inc. (US). AP will issue a PO referencing Nova Health, Inc. and will attach the tax certificate to payments.

We accept the activation fee proration language as proposed. Please send the final signed order form and invoice remit details so AP can set up the vendor and schedule the first payment.

Ella

Attachments referenced in thread: OrderForm_NovaHealth_v2_redline.docx; Nova_2026_Tax_Certificate.pdf
